text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly firmer on Wednesday, traders said.
Gas oil was slightly firmer although many traders were cautious after the reclosure of the arbitrage to the Far East.
Two 45,000 tonne 0.2 percent cargoes were reported to have traded over the past two days at fob hi +$1.20 and +$1.50 for end of the month delivery.

Traders speculated that the cargoes had been earmarked for delivery into a recent Indian tender but closure of the arbitrage could mean they would be diverted into West Africa and possibly the Middle East.
An Italian player was reported to have sold a one percent sulphur 20,000 tonne cargo at fob hi +25 cents
EN590 was also a little firmer with an Italian Islands cargo recently sold for fob high +$3.75 for end of the month delivery. Premiums were generally assessed at fob hi +$3.0/+$4.0.
Gasoline rose $2 on the back of firmer NWE values and tight local supplies, especially premium unleaded, traders said.
One source bullish on the Med cited Romanian cargoes moving into Turkey and higher than expected Italian demand in June.
"The Med on a prompt basis is tight," the source said. "It's a two-tiered market. For 95 unleaded, it's blanced to tight.
"For low run, it's a bit dodgy, but supported by Turkey."
"The Med is much stronger than the rest of Europe," the source said, but acknowledged there was very little demand from Nigeria. The arb to the U.S. was shut, the source said.
Naphtha rose a notional $3 in line with the sharp rise in NWE prices. An Egyptian Alex cargo now on the water traded at $186.75 cif basis Rotterdam to arrive June 16, sources said.
One source said the Med was quiet, with little demand expected until later in the month.
High sulphur fuel oil cargoes were steady with traders saying that an 18,000 tonne loader of ISAB specification material was sold at $75.25 fob on Tuesday.
However one trader said bearish sentiment was coming into the market as Electricidad de Portugal, a major buyer of high sulphur cargoes, will not be taking any material in July.
One seller was said offering Russian M-100 at $83 cif.
